utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sayers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Sayers: [Cont'd]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Major. Just for the Trial Chamber's information, we had reached towards the end of paragraph 26 of the summary signed by Major Ljubas. Major, is it the case that one mobile unit of the ABiH called the El Mujahed Unit was stationed in Travnik just before the offensive launched by the ABiH on June -- on around June the 3rd to the 8th of 1993?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, there was a Mujahed unit there, and it was quartering together with the 7th Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it the case that there were about 120 to 150 Mujahedin in the nearby village of Mehurici who used to parade and drive around purely Croat villages, waving flags and singing religious songs, intending thereby to harass and intimidate the local Croat population?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In a locality called Mehurici, 120 to 150 Mujahedin were stationed permanently, and others were stationed in surrounding villages in Muslim houses and used to gather in the mosques. And from those localities and their seat in Mehurici, they would take vehicles to drive around Croat localities, carrying green and red flags and singing some unknown -- some unfamiliar songs and intimidating the Croat population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Major. We can pass over paragraphs 27 and 28 of your outline here, because you've already testified about those matters yesterday. Let me draw your attention to June the 3rd, 1993, and the events that accompanied the launching of the large offensive against the HVO and Croat civilians in the Travnik and Novi Travnik area. Where were you stationed during the early days of this offensive, Major?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My command post was in Dolac, so my headquarters were in Dolac, and at times I was at the command post and at times I was visiting the troops who were along the front lines facing the army of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe it's accurate to say, Major, that many of the Croat houses in Dolac were burned down to the ground and all of them were looted and vandalised, and that several civilians were killed, and among the buildings that were vandalised was the church in Dolac which was desecrated by the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All of the attacks and snipers began to work as of the 3rd of June, and the first victims fell on the 3rd of June. The first Croats were killed in the direction of the church. As I said, I believe that as many as 12 civilians died on that day, killed by the snipers from surrounding villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In paragraph 30 of your summary, you talk about the fiercest ABiH series of attacks occurring on June the 8th, 1993. Could you tell the Trial Chamber, in your own words, what occurred on that day, Major?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fiercest attack of the Muslim units took place on the 8th of June. That was a terrible day for Croats, because on that day alone 92 Croats were killed, including 24 members of the HVO and 68 civilians. In that area, many houses were set on fire. There were also women and children killed and old people who were also killed. It was the worst day for the Croats in the municipality of Travnik and the whole of the Lasva Valley. As I have already pointed out, those who should have protected -- who could protect this population were on the front lines against the army of the Republika Srpska, so that the population were left to fend for themselves. And that is why so many of them perished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Major. You've already testified that your brigade commander in the Travnicka Brigade was Jozo Leotar, and I believe that you found out through him that Colonel Blaskic, the Operative Zone commander, had ordered the HVO to withdraw from the town of Travnik and from the municipality, and that all Croat civilians in the outlying villages and in Travnik were to be evacuated towards Nova Bila.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My commander, Jozo Leotar, told me about the reports from the ground about the victimisation of the civilian population. I learned that Colonel Blaskic had ordered to protect the civilians and to take them to a safe place around Nova Bila, that is, an area which would be safe for the Croat population in that part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two small facts, Major. It's true, I gather, by June the 7th of 1993, the ABiH had established complete military control over the town of Travnik and neighbouring Croat villages.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the 7th, 8th, until about the 13th. That was the period of very fierce fighting, and at that time the Armija succeeded to take both the town of Travnik and surrounding villages with the majority Croat population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the fighting spread down to Novi Travnik, as far down south as that as well, did it not?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as I have already said. We had, as I already listed, the concentration of large forces around Travnik, so when they took Travnik and surrounding Croat places, then the BH army extended -- expanded its attacks in the direction of Novi Travnik also.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it the case that by June the 14th of that year, the ABiH had established full control over the main Travnik-Zenica road as far east of Travnik as Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is, until about the 14th, the BH army managed to take control of the Travnik-Guca Gora road on to Zenica. That is the road along which there were mostly Croat localities and Croat populations, which was then expelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: With the Trial Chamber's permission, we have a short video clip taken by the BBC, I believe, during the Travnik offensive. It lasts about two minutes, Your Honour, and we have a transcript prepared for the Court, the Prosecution, and Mr. Cerkez' counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. [Videotape played].

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Exhibit number please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The videotape will be marked D217/1 and the transcript D217A/1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, you saw some contemporaneous videotape of events that surrounded the ABiH offensive and we also saw some comments made by then lieutenant, now Brigadier Duncan. Can you give your own perspective, sir, on the impact of this offensive on the local civilian Croat population in the Travnik municipality?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as you can see what was shown here now, you could see the civilian population is fleeing in panic, fearing another offensive. And you saw just one of the roads that the Croats, that is the civilian population, found running for their lives. So you could see people on the run carrying only in some small bags the minimum of their personal belongings. There were several directions which they took in their flight through Travnik, through Vilenica, trying to find shelter in the direction of Novi Travnik and Nova Bila. Here you could also see some units. These units, these men were on the front lines against Republika Srpksa, and they were very anxious. They were very concerned about the fate of their families. When they learned that so many houses had been burned, that people were running away, then they turned back to go home and see what had befallen their families, and to see how to protect the largest possible number of civilians so that the least possible number of civilians is victimised, to try to put them in a safe place. It was only when we were sure about that then we turned to the other part, that is how to stop that offensive in the best possible way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, a suggestion has been made in this case that these civilians were fleeing as a result of propaganda issued by the HVO or by political institutions of Bosnian Croat political parties rather than under the guns of the ABiH. Could you give your perspective on that, having been there yourself and seen it and heard things with your own -- seen things with your own eyes and heard things with your own ears?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could see it until the 3rd of June or rather the 8th. We could not go along with a basis that fighting could break out between Croats and Muslims. Nonetheless, it turned out that ever since the assassination of my commander, Ivica Stojak, to all those incidents in the former half of 1993, they showed clearly --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question was really not that. It was a rather simpler question. Were the Croat civilians fleeing as a result of propaganda or in fear of their lives? You were there. Tell us, please.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no propaganda. The civilians were on the run. The civilians took flight because they were being killed, harassed, ill treated, fearing, and they were running for their lives and the lives of their families.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me take you very briefly through paragraph 32, Major. We've heard from several witnesses that about 20.000 Croats civilians were expelled from the Travnik municipality. Would you concur with that figure?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: More than 300 Croat civilians were killed, 900 more wounded, and many massacres of civilians committed by ABiH troops. Would you concur with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. More than 300. When those offensives reached -- and more than 20.000 fled, and towards the end that number doubled. A large number of civilians and HVO members were wounded. Over 1.000 were wounded in the course of all those attacks of the ABiH army in its offensives.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The final exhibit, if I may, Your Honour, is a document that we received just yesterday from the United Nations Centre for Human Rights, and it describes the impact of the offensive on the surrounding villages and a certain number of massacres that were committed by ABiH troops. I'd like to take the Major through it, if I may, and I'd like to get an exhibit number for it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will be marked D218/1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sayers, I simply would like, regarding this testimony or the testimony we heard yesterday which was a very moving one, and this present testimony, I would like to remind you of what we said. We are not presently looking into any situation of tit-for-tat of retaliation. We are very removed from that concept. We're dealing with a very specific trial, and we shouldn't steer away from that. I'd like to remind you of that. This is a constant reminder. It is important to see what perspective we're working in.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and we have that in mind and I think that the presentation of our evidence is going to keep that in mind. As I said in the opening statement, we just had a few examples of municipalities such as Travnik, Kakanj, and Bugojno, just to illustrate the point of who was really doing what to whom. The allegation in this case, in count one against Mr. Kordic anyway, is that there was a pervasive policy of persecution against Bosnian Muslims by Bosnian Croats in the territory of the HZ HB and the HR HB and in the municipality of Zenica. We've covered largely Zenica to this point, and this evidence is going to really who is really persecuting whom in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You are just picking out two or three samples and will you limit yourself to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Absolutely. We have in mind the Court's observations regarding, as you put it, tit-for-tat atrocities. Just because one person commits an atrocity doesn't justify another one. We're very well aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, this is a document as a result of the commission at the United Nations Centre for Human Rights visiting the Brajkovici parish on the 18th of June, 1993. I know you can't speak English, but let me just take you through the high points of this document. On the second page, the commission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just one moment so we can understand it. It appears to be a translation of the report of a Christian Information Service on this matter rather than a report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I think that is correct, indeed, Your Honour. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What we have here Major is a commission of the Christian Information Service that visited Brajkovici on the 18th of June 1993 and is reported on in a United Nations Centre for Human Rights report in July. The commission describes a visit to the village of Susanj in Zenica where about 100 houses were emptied, a number of civilians were detained, mostly old women and children, and a listing of 16 persons known to have been killed. Did you know anything, yourself, about atrocities committed in the village of Susanj? Did you ever hear about that in the period of June, July, 1993, sir?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know better are other villages adjacent to Susanj. About Susanj, specifically, I cannot say anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let's just go down the list of villages in Travnik municipality. How about the village of Ovnjak, do you know about killings in that village or a killing in that village and the looting of Croat houses?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the village of Grahovcici, according to this report, four people were known to have been killed, four civilians and all 200 houses of that village were empty with the inhabitants having been chased to Nova Bila. Is that consistent with your recollection of what happened in Grahovcici during this period, sir?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am aware of what is said here in this report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going down the list, in the village of Dolac and Bila in Travnik municipality, two people, two civilians killed, all 65 houses empty, the inhabitants having been chased to Nova Bila. Is that consistent with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This Dolac is near the mine of Bila, so it's in the direction of Han Bila, simply to avoid the confusion, because there is Dolac at Dilaca [phoen] and this is Dolac at Bila near the mine, Han Bila.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I may, just for the Court, I won't be asking questions about the village of Podovi which is on the bottom of page two or the incident on the second to last page regarding all of the executions at Bikosi, because we have submitted an affidavit of Pavo Barac, Your Honour, in cooperation with the testimony of Major Ljubas, and the affidavit is of a young fellow who was actually at those places when the killings occurred. But travelling on, sir, the commission reports about 18 civilian deaths in the village of Cukle. Were you familiar with those events in June and July of 1993?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the next page, the village of Brajkovici. The commission apparently determined -- it said that six people, six civilians had been killed and 100 houses apparently had been left vacant. Is that consistent with your recollection of what happened there?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just to take this very quickly, the village of Novo Selo and the village of Konjevici, one in Travnik municipality, one in Zenica, houses burned down, some re-occupied by Muslims, and Croat inhabitants chased out of those village. Is that consistent with your recollection of events in that terrible time?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is Novo Selo near Dolac, yes, then that is what it was like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, of your own knowledge, there were about 36 dead and missing people in Maljine; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And another seven people killed in Guca Gora that were buried at the monastery?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We exhumed them last year and gave them a proper burial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you understand, sir, at this time, that similar offensives were being launched by the ABiH in the Kakanj area?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through my chain of command, I received information that in addition to the offensive of the BH army in the municipality of Travnik, that it was also launching similar offensives in the municipalities of Novi Travnik, Zenica, Kakanj, and all those areas. And we heard that a large number of civilians had been victimised, many houses put to fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as far as you were aware, sir, was there any official or unofficial policy or recommendation of persecution or harassment of Muslim civilians by the HVO in Travnik or any neighbouring municipality?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was no such policy. I never carried out such policy, nor am I aware that any member of the HVO or the Croat part ever pursued such policies. The truth was quite the reverse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever receive any orders to persecute, harass, intimidate anyone from any other ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My explicit orders were to organise the front line against the army of Republika Srpska, that is, to organise the shifts and defence of the Lasva Valley against the army of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any soldiers under your command, as far as you know, actually, regardless of the existence or nonexistence of such a policy, actually engage in a practice of harassing or intimidating, roughing up people of non-Croat ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My members never received such orders, nor were any of them active in any policy of persecution, ill treatment, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Major. No further questions. Cross-examined by Mr. Mikulicic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Ljubas. Representing Mr. Cerkez, I'm going to ask you a few short questions, and please answer them to the best of your recollection. Mr. Ljubas, yesterday in the examination-in-chief, you described how you became organised, how in 1992 the units evolved. Is it true that throughout 1992, up until the offensive ABiH in June 1993, the only and exclusive objective of the organisation of your units was the defence against the army of Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that in this period, until the attack of June 1993, you, as a soldier, had no military objectives with respect to the army of Bosnian Muslims?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ljubas, yesterday you mentioned that you know that the ABiH officers Mr. Cuskic and Mr. Alagic arrived from Croatia to the area of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ljubas, do you know whether Messrs. Cuskic and Alagic, before arriving in Bosnia, were fighting against the JNA on the Croatian side?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that with their arrival, the incidents in the Travnik area intensified?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you illustrate this claim?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. With the 1st and 7th Krajina Brigades, which were then merged into the 17th Krajina Brigade, led by Messrs. Cuskic and Alagic, we all expected that their forces and their equipment, because they were well equipped, would be put to use against the army of Bosnian Serbs so that we could try to take back the town of Jajce. But this did not happen. Their forces started deploying in surrounding villages, whereas they were first in the barracks in Travnik. So the relations were disrupted. There were provocations, power was being cut off, water and telephone lines, because they controlled them. One of their command posts was in Plave Vode, which was the source of potable water for the whole area. Then checkpoints were set up by these units, and yesterday I pointed out that certain HVO members and civilians were killed there, and I was disarmed at one of those checkpoints. So there was abuse which they carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Ljubas. You said that the units led by Cuskic and Alagic were very well equipped.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Trial Chamber has already heard that these units arrived in about 20 buses which had Croatian registration plates. Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the registration plates, but I saw the buses as they were arriving in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you also know the fact that these units were also equipped in the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, these units arrived fully equipped in buses from the direction of the Republic of Croatia. How they became equipped, where they got it, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To join the joint struggle against the Bosnian Serbs was their principal task?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and we were looking forward to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ljubas, yesterday you also said that in the beginning, organisationally speaking, the HVO was better prepared because they saw the threat from the JNA sooner, but that later on the ABiH, the army of Bosnian Muslims, also prepared well and that they had a number of professional officers who had gotten their training with the JNA.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is true that the ABiH had more trained officers who had come from the JNA than the HVO did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Speaking of the two gentlemen, Fikret Cuskic and Mehemed Alagic, can you confirm that they were also professional soldiers trained in the former JNA?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ljubas, can you confirm that in the area of Travnik, Refik Lendo and Bislim Zurapi were also active, and they had come from the JNA?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that. This was Novi Travnik, and it was a different zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that in your zone of responsibility in Travnik, the former Mr. Ahmet Kulenovic was also a former JNA officer?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ljubas, yesterday you mentioned that the ABiH received military equipment. This is also mentioned in paragraph 16 of your statement. Equipment which arrived from Islamic countries; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how this equipment arrived? Was it by road?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that these road transports in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina entered the country through the territory of the Republic of Croatia, all from the west, south-west?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, they came from the south, going up to Central Bosnia. I don't know the details of how they reached that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you couldn't tell us anything more about that. Very well, Mr. Ljubas. That concludes my questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I didn't realise that counsel had finished. Cross-examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, you've given extensive evidence about Travnik, without notes, and giving figures and matters of detail. Have you been able to refresh your memory, before coming here, from any documents?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So all the figures that you've provided, where did they come from?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are figures which I use on a daily basis, given my current duties, figures that I know from the time when the events occurred; for instance, numbers which we added up when we were burying people, for instance, in the dark days which are not easy to forget because they are some of the worst days for my people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us that you started off in 1990 as a member of the political party, and you've remained a member of that party every since.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I became a member of this party, and when the HVO was established, I froze my membership and I did nothing else, because then I became a professional officer, and this is the post that I still hold.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us about the division between the military and the civilian part of the HVO. That's from your personal knowledge and experience, is it?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the area where I was, that is, in Nova Bila.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then, of course, your knowledge and experience of Travnik generally in your various roles in the army?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat, please? I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've got knowledge of Travnik generally. You've given us extensive evidence of what was happening in Travnik, and this comes from your experience in the army, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all the experience that I have. I was born in Travnik, I grew up in Travnik, I went to school in Travnik, and also it is based on everything that I experienced in the war. So this is all my personal experience.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've spoken of Mr. Kordic. What do you say was his role, if any, in the affairs of the HVO at Travnik?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, Mr. Kordic was an active politician. And as far as the military side is concerned, I personally had no contact, nor did Mr. Kordic have any influence over me or my unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a deputy and then as a commander, you got to know how the war was being run, at least to a degree you got to know that; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which part of the war are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The part that concerned Travnik.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the war run against the forces of the army of Republika Srpska and, later on, against the attacks of the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I wonder if the witness could have a brief look at Exhibit Z50.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is not in your language, I'm afraid. It's a document prepared by some of the European Monitors, and it relates to February 1992, so quite early on. But you were already involved, and it speaks of how there was a meeting first at Travnik with various people named, the mayor of Travnik, Professor Udovicic, Mr. Solsic, Mr. Topalovic, and how the meeting moved on to Donja Puticevo, where Mr. Kordic, as vice-president of BH, was present. Do you remember those early meetings of Monitors coming to meet people in Travnik and Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall this meeting, and I wasn't present there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Under paragraph 2 of the meeting, and I'm sorry it's in English but I'll read it slowly insofar as it's material, at Novi Travnik it says: "There was a roadblock of 150 uniformed men in Croatian camouflage uniforms, with Croatian cap symbols and with HOS markings." Does that fit with your recollection of what was going on at about that time in your area?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I was not in Novi Travnik. If you followed me closely yesterday, I said that on the 27th of February, we attempted to establish a unit of Sveti Duh in Nova Bila in order to prevent the JNA to haul all the military equipment to Mount Vlasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But at about this time, which is one of the reasons I ask you about this particular document, the day after, you would have known what's going on. Is it the case that people wearing Croatian uniforms and symbols had set up a roadblock just down the road at Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you heard what I said yesterday, in this period, we had a very high morale in terms of organisation for defence but we were very poorly equipped. And in these attempts to stop the JNA convoys from taking out the equipment, people who were there, people who wanted to defend themselves were wearing whatever they had handy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Then may the witness see Z115, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Travnik War Presidency -- this, as you can see, from the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna Council in Busovaca, it's addressed to the Travnik War Presidency in Travnik. Now, you were based in Travnik at the time, correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I was in Dolac and I was at the front line against the army of Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us a great deal about Travnik. Can you help us with this? There's a request for MTS, equipment and materiel, to establish good quality necessary for communications with Busovaca HVO units. And a particular piece of communications equipment, I think, the repeater, is identified, and then a Mr. Florijan Glavocevic; do you know that man?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And a Mr. Jovanovic is referred to. Do you know that man?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it's signed for the HVO staff of Central Bosnia by Mr. Kordic. From all your dealings in Travnik, can you explain why Mr. Kordic would be specifically seeking this type of equipment from the Travnik War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you heard me, at that time, I was the commander of the 4th Company and as a company commander who was engaged in war against the Bosnian Serbs, this type of information is -- was not really available.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well. Well, let's look at another order. Exhibit 134, please. This is for the 15th of June of 1992. I think that this one must be withdrawn for the time being and come back later, although the original -- we'll just check it with the witness, but the original reads 1992, but I think it should be 1993 as the reference number in the documents suggests, and I'll deal with it in the appropriate time in the sequence. I'll come back to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is this the document about which we had some evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. So I'll put it back to its rightful place in June 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll have a document for you to look at shortly if necessary, but on the 23rd of August of 1992, there was a swearing in of officers in Travnik, I think, is that correct, and soldiers?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat the date, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 23rd of August, I suggest.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 23 August. I need to be refreshed further. I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the swearing in ceremony itself in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I cannot recall. If you can give me some specific detailed -- the exact time or the exact place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you take part, yourself, in a swearing-in ceremony?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you perhaps help me where that oath-taking ceremony took place?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time, apart from the fact that it's in Travnik, no, I can't. We may have to come back to it. But just think back, please. You became a soldier. You were in charge of other soldiers. Was there an oath-taking ceremony?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I had a lot of problems with the army of Bosnian Serbs. It was very difficult to organise a front line, to organise logistics service which was very poor, so I don't know much about any ceremonies. I didn't have much time or take part in any of this. So this is why I'm saying if you can further refresh my memory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In August 1992, would your unit still be the Sveti Duh, the Holy Ghost unit?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In August?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said the unit of the Holy Ghost existed until the 8th of April, until the establishment of the HVO, and then I was assigned to the post of commander of the 4th Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, then I'll come back to that when I've got the document after the break. It may be before. May the witness please see Exhibit 229.1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're from Travnik and here's a document that deals with the appointment of someone called Marinko Palavra to the job of commander of the Special Purpose Unit of the police administration. Now, it sets out the reasoning for the appointment and it sets out the approval of the deputy president of HZ HB, Mr. Kordic; and the secretary-general, Mr. Kostroman; and then, Mr. Pervan. From your knowledge of Travnik, does all this fit that Mr. Kordic should be approving of the appointment of people in Travnik even at that time in September of 1992?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This refers to the civilian police and police affairs, and this is not something that I am familiar with from that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, as a deputy commander and then as a commander, you must have had some contact with some politicians from time to time.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As commander of a company, I could not have had contact with the civilian structures because the level of company does not allow this. In addition, I had specific tasks in organising the defence line against the army of Republika Srpksa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just before we move on in time, quite swiftly, who was actually running the war? You've spoken of the military line of command, but who was giving the military their instructions?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that there was a chain of command. As a company commander, I had my own commander which was a battalion commander, and he received it up from the brigade commander, and the brigade commander received it in his turn from the Operative Zone commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, but one only has to turn on the news or look back over history to realise that many if not most or all wars have a political control or element. Now, you were involved for a long time in Travnik as you have explained to us. Did the military superiors of yours or even the military officers at your rank and below know and discuss who was actually making the fundamental decisions about how the war was being conducted?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had our chain of command which we respected. And the highest level of command, it was the head of the main staff, the commander of the Operative Zone. Who they were in contact with, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us of the distinction between the civil, as you say, and military parts of the HVO. The civil part has to have a function and -- or were you saying it was entirely subordinate to the military part?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You're not suggesting this was, as it were, a military rule. This was rule in some way by politicians, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was no dictatorship. The army had its specific task to organise the front line and the defence and the civilian part was responsible for food supplies, medicine supplies, and the protection of the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I may come back to that. On the 21st of October of 1992, where were you?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 21st of October? As I said, on the 21st of October, 1992, the commander, my commander, the commander of the municipal staff, the Travnik staff, was killed so that was the time when we were trying to best organise his funeral without disrupting by this the front line against the army of Republika Srpksa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you doing?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I was the commander of the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you doing the funeral or were you leading your soldiers? Were you at the front?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I led my -- I was leading my soldiers and the brigade command to care for the funeral. But, since I was the commander, of course I had to pay my last respects to my late commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wonder if I could ask for your comment on our Exhibit 243, please. While we're coming to that, we've got a map of the front -- perhaps we'll get it up again but -- perhaps at the break. But the front you're speaking of is the northwestern front, isn't it, between the Serb forces and your forces?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the northwestern part of the town of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Running to and close to Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Travnik and Novi Travnik are neighbouring municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if you could just have the first page, please, in front of you. Put it on the ELMO. This is describing the situation at the Novi Travnik front on the 21st of October with Muslim forces aiming at the town of Novi Travnik. Reference to the Muslim forces in Opara and other villages and so on. Then it comes down to the next paragraph which is HVO units setting out the blockade of roads to Novi Travnik and various other details. This is all very close to your area and if we go on to paragraph ten right at the end, it says this, "While defence operations are being conducted, the vice-president of Herceg-Bosna, Dario Kordic, and I are in Novi Travnik continuously leading the military operations with deep knowledge of the situation and by keeping all the forces under control. Commander Colonel Filip Filipovic is also here at the Novi Travnik HVO HQ." Now this is really down the road or around the corner from you, isn't it? Do you remember that happening?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, at that time, as I have said, I was the commander of the battalion and I was involved in organising the front line against the army of Republika Srpksa. At the time when my commander was killed and during the break, that is when I came back from the front line. I managed to pay my last respects to my commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, does the presence of Kordic along with Blaskic and Filipovic at the front line come as a surprise to you or not?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not -- at that time, I was not in that area so I cannot say anything about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying you never heard anything about his coming to the front line?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who are you referring to, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To Mr. Kordic. Are you saying you didn't hear of him coming to the front line?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my line? To my front line? I personally never saw Mr. Dario Kordic on my part of the front. About other parts, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The question was whether you ever heard of him coming to the front line.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot make guesses. I cannot say yes or no, he never -- he did not come to my front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you understand, Major, that you can tell us what other people told you? You've told us a great deal about villages and people and all sorts of things that I don't think you saw yourself. You can tell us what you have been told by others. Did anybody else ever tell you of Kordic going to the front line?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I heard about Mr. Kordic, I heard about Mr. Kordic, that when over 20.000 people, Croats from Travnik, from Zenica and from other places, fled, then I heard that he turned up amongst those civilians in an attempt to help them and do something about their accommodation. That I know because I heard it from my members whose families used to live in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, and the last time, the front line, "yes" or "no", did you hear of him there?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat that question, please? What do you mean, "the front line"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "The front line" is the phrase you've been using, and you described it for us. Did you hear of Mr. Kordic ever being at the front line?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm now in a position to come back in time to deal with the swearing-in ceremony. And it may be that the date is wrong, but you'll be able to help us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can the witness have, please, Exhibit 193.2. It's an example of a document where the original appears to have either degraded or for some other reason it's not possible at the moment to get a better copy of the original. I'll explore that over the break.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I think you're going to find, Major, that the original is only legible in a few places, and if I'm going to be able to get you a better version of this, it won't be until after the break. But I would like your comments in any event. The Holy Ghost 1st Company, the Sveti Duh 1st Company, is that a company of the group of which you were the commander?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not the commander of the Holy Ghost Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just explain, then, a little bit about the Holy Ghost Company? You had something to do with Sveti Duh, and it's my mistake for not understanding what it was.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a member of that unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Well, now forget the date, in case the date is incorrectly recorded. If you would look, please, at the document which is the first of the documents in Croatian or B/C/S, which begins "Stovana gospodo". Do you have that document in front of you? It's the one that is legible, as opposed the ones that aren't. Do you have that document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is an English translation of that, which the Chamber will be aware. And this, I'm suggesting to you, is the text of a speech that was read out at the swearing-in ceremony, and you can read it to yourself. But if the English version is on the ELMO, I'll read some of it, in any event. It's to: "Esteemed gentlemen, soldiers, NCOs, and officers of the Holy Ghost 1st Company, and esteemed gentlemen whom we've invited to distinguish this celebration of the anniversary of this unit's formation." Help us, please. The anniversary of the unit's formation, when would that give us as a date?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To begin with, the document that I have before me has no date and lacks all the other characteristics of an official document. But I said that the Holy Ghost Company was founded on the 27th of February, 1992, and the anniversary would then be on the 27th of February, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And it goes on to say: "We would like, on behalf of the Croatian Defence Council of Travnik municipality, to congratulate you on your first anniversary, with the hope that this unit, which operates as part of the Travnik Brigade, will continue to carry out successfully all military tasks which we place before it." And then it says: "A year ago, we formed this unit, with the task of preparing to defend its Croatian people in this area and in the areas of the Travnik municipality and our dear Herceg-Bosna." There is then a passage which was written and crossed out, which reads, underneath the crossings out, as follows: "The first weapons for this unit came from our dear Croatia and were organised by the Croatian Democratic Union, HDZ. You know that the first activists of the HDZ were from this area and that even today they constitute the backbone of this unit." Now, the paragraph may have been crossed out, but is what is said there true? Did the first weapons for the unit come from Croatia?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, with your leave, I cannot discuss this document because I am not familiar with this document. It is not signed or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just for a moment consider the question. It doesn't matter about the document. What counsel is putting to you is whether it's true that the first weapons for the unit came from Croatia. That was the question.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of that. The weapons that I received, I received through the war staff of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It also says, in the same paragraph, that: "You know that the first activists of the HDZ were from this area." Well, it may be a little ambiguous. Where do you say the first activists of the HDZ, which you joined, were from? Were they from the Travnik area?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first activists whom I joined were in the area where I lived, that is, the area of Nova Bila, and those were men who lived in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document goes on to say, as a person addressing the assembly would say: "We now have before us the Holy Ghost 1st Company, which is prepared to defend against aggressors of all kinds, and an aggressor is for us anyone who comes to our parts from outside without our agreement, regardless of nationality, whether Chetnik or Mujahedin. We have both in our territory, and we must fight them so that our dear Croatian people may stand proudly on its Croatian soil." Now, does that paragraph reflect the sort of sentiments of HVO or HDZ leaders in Travnik in, as you would say, the beginning of 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just object to this document. First of all, it's illegible and it's of dubious parentage. I think no foundation has been laid for it, and it's not right to cover documents the witness has never seen, in the absence of a proper foundation, and put to him propositions that are contained in there as if they were true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, who is it alleged made this speech?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If we come to the next document, I'll show how the document, as a whole, fits together. What you see on the second page in the English and what the witness can see on the next but mostly illegible page in the B/C/S, if he would like to turn to it, is that this is a proposal for the ceremony, with concrete activities, and there are various items set out there; the ceremony, the master of ceremonies, the details of various people taking part, and I was going to come to this later. Commander Ivo Stojak will receive the report, so the report -- the document to which this is attached is probably the report, and that would be from Mr. Ilija Nakic. He comes to the microphone, as you can see in the middle of the page, in front of the units, stands to attention, and then reports to him units of the Travnik for swearing in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The difficulty about it is, as counsel observes, it's illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I may or may not be able to deal with that over the break, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think you better before we continue with this cross-examination. As a matter of principle, illegible documents should not be produced. There must be, presumably, a better copy, or otherwise this translation couldn't have been done.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No. The only possibility, which is one I'll investigate over the break, is whether the original was an old-fashioned fax paper document that degrades over time, but I'll have that investigated. I'll come back to the document, with Your Honour's leave, later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I would like to ask the witness, having gone through this much so far, you see that what we've looked at so far relates to a unit of which you were familiar. Do you remember the ceremony concerning that unit now?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Let me just make an additional objection, Your Honour. The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, the question has been put. We'll come back to the document in a moment. Now, are you objecting to the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The objection is connected with the document, Your Honour. Let me sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll deal with the document after the break.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the ceremony concerning the unit with which you were familiar?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may, the 21st is mentioned here, that at that time Ivica Stojak was already dead, and this document says that Ivica Stojak attended that ceremony. And it puzzles me, so that I cannot answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The question is: Do you remember yourself, whatever the date is, whatever the correct date, do you remember a ceremony of this sort?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The anniversary ceremony?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Any sort.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this document, I don't really know it. But, yes, we did mark the anniversaries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You did.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I do not remember what it says here, because it's illegible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, but this was not the question that was put to you. Please leave the document aside. Don't worry about it any longer. But do you remember taking part in a ceremony, in an oath-taking ceremony, around a solemn celebration of some kind of anniversary, giving it some kind of religious character? This is the question that is being put to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'll come back to that later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't know that I need trouble you with this particular document, which is already an exhibit. In fact, I think I can satisfy myself that I needn't. No, I don't think I'll ask you about that. Is a man called Mladen, who became deputy chief of police, known to you?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to know his surname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would need to know his surname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a man called Tolo Mladen.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the beginning of 1993, were you spending time in Travnik as well as at the front line?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In early 1993, I was on the front line facing the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Coming back to Travnik from time to time?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would come to Travnik, as the battalion commander would come to Travnik in the evening for briefings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All I wanted was your observation -- and it's one of the outstanding exhibits, Your Honour, so that it's in 353.2 -- your observation on the fact that the appointment of a man as deputy chief of police would require Mr. Kordic's approval. Did you know anything about the organisation of events in Travnik that would fit with that, Mr. Kordic being involved at that level of detail?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I am not familiar with Mr. Kordic's activities or the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you -- and again I'm asking you these questions because you tell us you have a good memory -- where were you on the 20th or the 21st of January of 1993?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 20th of January -- could you repeat, please? I did not hear the year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 20th and 21st of January of 1993.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said at that time I was with my unit facing the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May we look at 534.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: After this, we'll adjourn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This comes from the defence department of the Travnik defence administration. Now, are you saying that's the civil part of the HVO, or is that the military of the HVO, a defence department?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The defence department is attached to the civil part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But we see here that this is an order to go to the chiefs of the municipalities of defence offices in Travnik, Novi Travnik, Vitez, Zenica, and Vares, and is the aim of committing available resources to the defence of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and the order which comes from the chief of the defence administration, Anto Puljic, is to those various municipality chiefs to acquaint themselves with activities that are to be carried out in connection with the formation or reorganisation of brigades and to have discussions with the president of the Croatian Defence Council, to update -- number 2, to update lists of assignments of military conscripts; number 3, to organise a mobilisation system for brigades; and, 4, to inform the chief of the Travnik defence administration of the execution of those orders. There was no real division between military affairs and civil affairs, was there? It necessarily was all part of the same single operation; isn't that the truth?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not the truth. The civil and the military part, activities, were separate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you accept that the content of this order is military in nature?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in touch with this order, and I am not familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, you've told us about almost every aspect of Travnik military and social history over the two-year period, and much of it no doubt drawn on what others told you. Please help us. Is this a military order or is it not? You were a soldier.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If you are familiar with the affairs of defence administrations and offices, these administrations are responsible for the civil part, that is, registering and mobilising men and materiel. That is the civilian part which engages in registering and mobilising, calling up men of military age. And as for the military part, it has nothing to do with the operative command or leadership.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Will that be a convenient moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll adjourn now for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone to the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can we return to the question of the document. I think it was an outstanding objection that Mr. Sayers was going to raise. But subject to that, I'm in a position to produce the originals held here which, although on one page certainly it's hard to read and in part, I think, impossible, the rest of it is now substantially legible although difficult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let us see them and then we'll pass them on to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: They come in two separate envelopes. Can you just give me a minute? I've mucked something up. I'm just going to put it right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sayers. Well, that is a much lore legible copy than anything we've got in our exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I absolutely agree, Your Honour. The only other objection that I wanted to make was this: According to page four of the English document, the English version right at the top, and this is legible in the Croatian, I believe, 23 Kolovoz in the Croatian; 23rd of August in the English. The Major has already testified that the anniversary of the founding of this company, and he testified on page 34, lines 15 to 17, that the company was founded on February 27th, 1992. So the anniversary of it would have to be February 27th, 1993, by which time Ivica Stojak had been dead for four months according to the witness' testimony. So in the absence of a better foundation that this ceremony actually occurred rarely than merely being proposed as is indicated in the agenda, I'm afraid we have to maintain our objection to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, there is something in that point. In the absence of any other evidence that it actually took place, it really is simply in evidence that it is proposed, as it is said.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, as to an anniversary, that is a matter that, of course, goes only to weight, because we have this witness saying when this unit was formed, but I don't think we have any other document showing it. Indeed, we have no documents from this witness as from nearly all the Defence witnesses, so the date point doesn't really have any weight. The witness has himself acknowledged the occurrence of events like this, the 23rd of August seems -- which was the day I originally put to him and, perhaps I should have stuck to it more firmly because it's much more likely the date. And I'm interested in asking him further questions about the content of what was to be said or what was said and about the people who attended. Because it's of significance to discover from contemporaneous documents what was the attitude of participants at the time, and in my respectful submission, this document enables me properly to ask those matters and, in due course, for the Chamber to weigh the answers that are given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We shall admit the document on this basis: It is, of course, not evidence that the ceremony took place or as to a date or anything of that sort; none of that being clear from it. However, it is a proposal and counsel is entitled to ask questions about it, as he says, in order to obtain evidence as to what the attitudes of the people were at the time and as to whether there was a proposal to have a ceremony of this sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May the witness therefore have before him the originals that we have because they are more legible or at least the original of the four-page document because that's more legible than the earlier version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, we're going back in time, it would appear, to the 23rd of August or thereabouts of 1992. And if you look at the document, most of it legible now, you'll see it's headed, "A Proposal for the Ceremony." And I needn't trouble you with most of the detail except to remind you, as you observed to us, that Mr. Stojak is referred to there. There's the reference to playing the anthem -- I'm looking at the headlines of the paragraphs -- with speed, and raising the flag. There's reference to what will be said by the master of ceremonies. And then we can see, I don't know if you've got -- if you're looking through it quickly to help us, we can see that the ceremony is to end with an address by Mr. Kordic. I think you remember the anniversaries were celebrated. Do you remember Mr. Kordic attending?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone to the witness.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I said, the Holy Ghost Company existed barely a month and a half, and then from there until the end of the war, it was never re-established or anything. And I said when these ceremonies took place. They are now in place after the war to mark certain important dates. I don't know this document, this proposal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Kordic attend these ceremonies, or some of them, to be the last and, in a sense, the major speaker?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the ceremonies which I attended were the ones after the war. During the war, I was at the front line, so that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In which case, can we look briefly at the other document. If you would put those four sheets in that green file, and we can look at either the other file or the earlier version of the page of the speech. If you would bring me the material, I'll show what to show the witness. That page there, that's the only one. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, assume, if you'll be good enough, that this document may relate to the middle of 1992. Follow me, please. And I simply want your comment on whether the sentiments expressed here are the sort of sentiments you would expect to be being expressed in public in Travnik. I dealt with the Holy Ghost as defender against both the Chetnik and the Mujahedin. Then this: "The sacred goal of the Croatian people in this territory is the preservation of peace and coexistence with those who wish to live with us in our Croatian provinces in our Herceg-Bosna." In the middle of 1992, would that have been the sort of publicly-expressed view?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, there are two separate documents here. I think you've already made a ruling with respect to the first one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We admitted both. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You remember the question, please, Major. Is that the sort of --

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can see on the document, two thirds of the way down: "The sacred goal of the Croatian people in this territory is the preservation of peace and coexistence with those who wish to live with us in our Croatian provinces in our Herceg-Bosna." Is that the sort of publicly-expressed sentiment you would have expected?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you can see in the document which you're putting to me, this is 1993, and this is a salute to the officers and soldiers of the Holy Ghost Company, which at that time did not exist any longer, and it never came back into existence after it was absorbed into the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you one more question along the same lines. It may help you to answer the question, please, if you don't even bother to look at the document. It's a matter for you. Towards the bottom of the page, second-to-last, this sentiment: "The Mujahedin and the Chetniks cannot live in coexistence with us, and it is the Holy Ghost Company which must show the strength of Croatian soldiers." Would that be a sentiment that would have been current in 1992?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the period to which you're referring, in February and March of 1992, there was no mention of Mujahedin; nor did I mention that during the existence of the Holy Ghost Company, that there were any Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm not going to take it any further with this witness, Your Honour, the circumstances of his answers. Can the original documents, if they are not all back -- they are all back, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's a good example of what should happen to that document. I suppose you're proposing to take it back.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'll raise it with you at the end of the evidence or alternatively defer it, along with other issues, to Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Friday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, the position is that the HVO was a Croatian-based body, serving the interests of the Croats, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And inevitably it had an effect on non-Croats in Travnik, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For example, when we come to -- and I'm now moving back to where we were in the history of events -- to April of 1993, do you accept that in Travnik, Croatian flags were being flown and that they had an inflammatory effect?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree. I agree that the flags were flown, that the flags were raised during the Christian holidays, as they were during the Muslim holidays. Those did not bother the Croatian people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the flying of Croatian flags undoubtedly bothered the Muslim people, didn't it, because it represented a threat to them? Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not represent a threat, because this was normal for each ethnic group to raise their symbols on the occasions of their holidays.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the first document that I needn't trouble the witness with, I think, is 634.1, already admitted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, you would accept that a decision would have been made in Travnik by Mr. Pervan on the 9th of April to fly Croatian flags on certain particular buildings; the bus terminal, St. John's Church, and [indiscernible]; you would accept that that order would have been made, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who issued this order from the civilian structures, but I did see flags, and also I saw them being burned.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Then, Your Honour, it's Exhibit 635. It's a short passage, so I'll read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The ECMM monitors, Major, did you have any dealings with them?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I pointed out I was battalion commander with a specific task at the front line, and all other contacts were handled by the command at another level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, Major, you've been brought here as a witness to tell us nearly everything about Travnik, and I'm going to want your help on one or two of the things that the ECMM monitors have said. Do you know any reason to doubt the good faith of the ECMM monitors who were operating in your area?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot speak to the monitors' statements, because I was at the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to read you one monitor's report from the 9th of April. It is, as I say, Exhibit 635 for those who wish to see it in the original, and it says this: "Tensions rose in the evening when a Muslim apparently fired on a Croat who was erecting a Croat flag. This resulted in over an hour of fighting, but all was quiet by 2230." That would probably not be surprising to you. You would accept that, would you, Major?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you had listened to my statement, I said that on that date, 9 April, the Bosniaks had arrested prominent Croat citizens and placed them in the fort in the old town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was going to ask you about that in due course, and I'll come back to it. I still want your answer to my question, and I'll read you the rest of the quotation from the monitor. He said this: "A BiH officer blamed a visit by Mate Boban to Travnik yesterday, who complained about the lack of Croat flags." And he then went on, the ECMM monitor, to say: "Travnik will continue to have a high flash point, as it is a mainly Muslim area but the Vance-Owen Plan places it in a Croat area. This was the reason for sustained fighting in the area after the plan was publicised." Now, dealing with Boban's visit, any reason to doubt that what was reported by the BiH officer was true and that Boban visited and asked for more flags; any reason to doubt that, please?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware that the late Boban was in Travnik at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The comment about the effect of the Vance-Owen Plan which placed Travnik in a Croat area, despite its Muslim majority, do you accept you were there, that that was one of the causes of difficulty if not the principal cause of difficulty?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please be more specific? I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course. What the monitor suggested was that Travnik would have a high flash point, would be a difficult area, because it was mainly Muslim, but the Vance-Owen Plan placed it in a Croat area and that that was the reason for sustained fighting after the Vance-Owen Plan was publicised. Do you accept the monitor's comment as being accurate so far as you could judge things being the man from Travnik?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the census of 1991, 37 per cent of the population were Croats, and there were about 8.000 Serbs and about 5.000 or 6.000 of others, and the rest were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you did understand my question about what the monitor said, didn't you? About his saying that it was the Vance-Owen Plan and so on that caused or was a cause of the difficulty. You did understand my question?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not -- I am not really familiar with the Vance-Owen Plan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, Major, you answered not only Mr. Kordic's counsel's questions, in great detail in fluency, but also from Mr. Cerkez's counsel. Are you having difficulty following the questions I'm asking you?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to move on from that exhibit. From your position in Travnik, did you learn anything of Ahmici or not?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did I learn anything about Ahmici? Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what did you learn and from where?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, as I told you, I was on the front line facing the army of Republika Srpksa. But, at a later date, I learned that Ahmici had happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From whom did you learn that?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned the details after the war. After the war I learned that it had happened. Before that, I had enough problems on the front line, and I was not -- I did not know details of things that happened in other municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not going to pursue that with this witness. The next exhibit is 939.2. It's for the 18th of May of 1993, and it's a document from your Commander Leotar. This is an order dated the 18th of May from Leotar relating to an agreement in Sarajevo between Petkovic and Mladic to implement a mutual cease-fire at lines of contact between the HVO and the Serbian army. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it doesn't involve the BiH, does it?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've told you, we held more than two-thirds of the front against the army of Republika Srpksa, and such orders to cease hostilities were normal. It was to exchange the prisoners of war, those killed, those wounded and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I must suggest to you that your observation about holding two-thirds of the front line may or may not be true or may be true for a small portion of the line near Travnik, but that overall, the BiH held a far larger proportion of that front line than did the HVO. What would you say to that?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO LJUBAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said two-thirds of the front line, I meant the municipality of Travnik and I am familiar with those defence lines. I do not know about other defence lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
